newsitem.title: HONG KONG: New World Infra raises working capital.
newsitem.headline: New World Infra raises working capital.

text.p: New World Infrastructure Ltd plans to use the net proceeds of an issue of 84 million new shares for working capital, said Credit Lyonnais Securities Asia, which acted as lead manager for the issue.
"They were saying that it would be for working capital. They have many, many projects in the pipeline," said Gary Coull, chairman of Credit Lyonnais Securities Asia Ltd.
"The debt to equity ratio will fall from 45 percent to 19.5 percent. The fully diluted NAV (net asset value) rises by 1.6 percent to HK$20.50," he said, quoting Credit Lyonnais estimates.
New World Infrastructure parent New World Development Co Ltd placed 84 million existing shares at HK$24.30 on Tuesday before subscribing to the same amount at the same price, Credit Lyonnais said.
It said the placement of existing shares represented about 10.3 percent of New World Infrastructure's existing share capital.
"The deal was oversubscribed and it was done very quickly -- just under two hours. The demand from local retail and institutions was very strong. Demand overseas is also pretty good," said Coull.
Tai Fook Securities was also involved in the placement.
Coull said the new issue would dilute earnings per share "a little bit".
"The revised earnings per share growth is 28.7 percent compounded over three years," he said. But he said any new projects that New World Infrastructure planned would be earnings and NAV enhancing.
New World Infrastructure shares rose HK$0.45 on Tuesday to HK$25.05. New World Development shares fell HK$0.20 to HK$48.60.
